(2) The 14-day rule is our convention, not the dome's own — a defender can argue it is arbitrary. Mitigation: Section 6.15 documents the rule, applies it uniformly to twelve entries spanning ~64 days of silence range, and the rule errs on the conservative side (two weeks is a long window for any active project to post a one-line result on its own published prediction). (3) Could the silent-ignore pattern reverse after the next manual commit ends the drought? Possible, but the d~=59 manual drought is itself the cleanest behavioral signal — the dome project has gone two months without an author-touched commit; any reversal would be a substantive event we would analyze on its own merits at that time. (4) Is the d=15 heartbeat worth an AR at all? Yes — the daily AR series is the audit trail that proves we did not back-fill or rewrite the silence record after the fact; each day's AR is its own dated snapshot of what we knew on that day. The audit-trail value is structural even when the scientific content is null.
